judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'provide its support and written consent when required' is vague about what triggers the duty, but the approval mechanics are otherwise plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits ¶12's allocation of approval responsibilities and ¶12's Brownfield approval paragraph without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'must be reasonable and necessary to affect Optionee's intended use' uses 'affect' for 'effect' and states a soft standard, but the drafting duties are clearly allocated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with ¶8 (Optionee estimates Eligible Activity costs) though ¶8 places the estimating burden on Optionee while this paragraph adds Optionor 'assistance' — a small overlap, not a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'obtain approval of the Brownfield Plan for the project prior to Optionee by no later than December 1, 2006' is garbled — 'prior to Optionee' has no referent — and 'so long as the delays are not caused by the Optionor' sits oddly with an extension exercisable by Optionor.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The December 1, 2006 deadline plus four 30-day extensions interacts with ¶12's later paragraph on retention of the Outstanding Balance if the Plan is not approved before Closing, and with ¶2's minimum one-year term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'that amount (up to the Limitation of Liability) shall be deducted' is ambiguous as to whether 'that amount' means the approved amount or the shortfall, which changes the deduction entirely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reuses ¶8's $500,000 'Limitation of Liability' for a second, different deduction against the Outstanding Balance, leaving unclear whether the cap is aggregate across ¶8 and ¶12.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'retained by Optionee' is odd on its own terms, since under ¶3 the Outstanding Balance is payable to Optionor out of TIF proceeds received by the Developer, not held by Optionee.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is hard to reconcile with ¶3 and ¶4, which make the Outstanding Balance a deferred Developer payment stream rather than escrowed funds in Optionee's hands, and with ¶13's assignment of the Option to the Developer.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'further assignment only with the prior written consent of the original Optionee' and 'in it sole discretion' (typo) are workable, though 'This Option may be assigned ... without the consent of the Optionor' is unqualified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: ¶1 limits assignment to 'Optionee's developer' prior to closing, while this paragraph permits assignment generally without Optionor consent — a genuine, if narrow, tension between the two.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'If Optionee elects not to exercise' makes termination turn on an unexpressed election rather than the passage of time, and 'without further action or obligation on the part of either party' is an unqualified sweep of uncertain reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It collides with ¶12's promise that if the Developer does not execute the purchase agreement Optionee will use best efforts to reimburse up to $50,000 in traffic-study costs, and with ¶2's open-ended 'not less than one (1) year' term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paragraph contains scanning/typing errors ('ferninine', 'the particular portion I which such word is used'), but the interpretive rules it states are conventional and the sense survives.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere — including ¶13's assignment terms — turns on partnership or agency status, so it is coherent with the whole.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'all acts as may be necessary' and documents 'in the form and substance satisfactory to the parties and their respective counsel' are broad, and the last sentence could swallow the obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports ¶16-style release recordings tied to Exhibit 3's recorded Memorandum, and no provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure boilerplate with a definite operation and no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere in the Option or Exhibit 3 bears on execution formalities.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The integration clause is clear, though it says the parties' agreements are 'embodied in this Option and Exhibit 1' while elsewhere naming Exhibit 3 as one of the only agreements — an internal wobble in one sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It omits Exhibit 2 (Survey) and Schedule A, both of which the Option incorporates by reference in ¶5 and ¶7(e), so the enumeration of documents is incomplete against the rest of the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Except as provided in the Act, all disputes arising under or relating to this Option shall be resolved under this Act' is slightly circular, but the CDA reference is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It names the same Contracting Officer as ¶20's notice address, so the two are consistent; the naming of an individual could be argued about if he left office.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause lists three delivery methods but supplies deemed-receipt rules only for mail and courier, leaving personal delivery unaddressed, and 'or is addressed in such other way as the parties may from time to time direct' is loose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: ¶2 makes exercise effective 'on the date of the receipt of notice ... as provided in Section 20', so the deemed-receipt gap here directly bears on when the Option is exercised and when Exhibit 1 becomes binding.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard time-of-the-essence clause with a clear weekend/holiday rule; nothing in it is ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Time of the essence is hard to reconcile with ¶2's open-ended 'not less than one (1) year' term, and with ¶12's Optionor-controlled extensions of the Brownfield deadline.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause demands a corporate resolution or partnership approvals but the Optionor is a Michigan limited liability company, so the required deliverable does not match the entity — a drafting mismatch.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble and Exhibit 3's acknowledgment identify Optionor as an LLC acting through a Managing Member, which this paragraph's corporate/partnership formula does not fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A recital-style identification of the parties with only typographical noise; nothing operative to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the Option's own preamble in date, parties and addresses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'containing 10.89 acres' is stated as exact and the Option is described as 'is fully assignable', both slightly firmer than the underlying grant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: ¶1 of the Option says 'approximately 10.89 acres' and describes the Property by reference to Exhibit 1, whereas this recorded Memorandum uses Attachment A — a recorded description that may not match the operative one.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It repeats verbatim the 'not less than one (1) year' formulation, which fixes a minimum but no expiration date, so the recorded instrument gives public notice of an option of indeterminate duration.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is meant to mirror ¶2 of the Option and does so, but that means the same open-ended term now appears in a recorded document, compounding rather than resolving the ¶2/¶14 problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short statement of recording purpose with a definite meaning and no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its reference to 'the Optionee or its assignee' is consistent with ¶1 and ¶13 of the Option on assignment.
